title: Farmers and supporters protest in Amritsar during Punjab bandh

tea.why: Protesters demonstrated during a statewide shutdown called over the killing of anti-drug activist Parminder Singh Jhota.
tea.want: Demonstrators demanded the resignation of the Chief Minister and DGP, an impartial probe into the murder, and strict action against drug trade networks.
tea.changed: Oct 15: Police detained five to seven individuals in Amritsar after they blocked roads and refused to clear paths for ambulances.

summary: Farmers and supporters gathered in Amritsar during a statewide Punjab bandh called to protest the murder of anti-drug activist Parminder Singh Jhota in Mansa. Organised by farmer groups and supported by political parties and the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee, participants blocked roads and burned an effigy of the state government at the Golden Gate. Protesters demanded the resignation of Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann and the DGP, as well as an impartial investigation into the killing and a crackdown on the drug trade. According to police reports, some demonstrations caused traffic disruptions that affected ambulances, prompting law enforcement to intervene. While most protesters dispersed following appeals from authorities, police detained between five and seven individuals who continued to block the roads.
demands: Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann to resign on moral grounds
Impartial investigation into Parminder Singh Jhota's murder
Action against those responsible for the drug trade
response: Police intervened to clear blocked roads and secure safe passage for ambulances, detaining 5 to 7 individuals who refused to comply. Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann promised strict punishment for those involved in the murder and asserted a zero-tolerance policy towards drug smuggling.
